criterion: error and rollback paths / partial-failure handling
finding: _update_list guards only a folder-shaped list file; other unusable list locations still raise raw errors from the writers
why: The round-6 fix claims every public call refuses with RepositoryListError, but add/remove/repoint still leak FileExistsError or PermissionError when ~/.afk is a file or the list file is unreadable, while reads give the clean error.
fix: Wrap the update_locked call in _update_list: catch OSError and re-raise RepositoryListError, and add a test where ~/.afk is a file.
evidence: ~/.afk is a regular file: lexists(list_file()) is false; safe_write._file_lock runs target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (safe_write.py:132) and raises FileExistsError from add_repository

finding: _update_list refuses a dangling symlink list file that the read path and safe_write both accept
why: os.path.lexists is true and os.path.isfile is false for a dangling symlink, so add/remove/repoint raise 'cannot be read: it is not a file', while _read_list returns [] and safe_write writes through the link target.
fix: Refuse only when the path exists and is not a file, or drop the pre-check.
evidence: if os.path.lexists(list_file()) and not os.path.isfile(list_file()): raise RepositoryListError("cannot be read: it is not a file", ...)

finding: Mutant lexists->exists in _update_list survives: no test puts a dangling symlink at the list file
why: The guard's use of lexists has no test, so it can be weakened to exists with every test still green.
fix: Add a dangling-symlink list-file test, or drop lexists.
evidence: mutant os.path.exists(list_file()) and not os.path.isfile(list_file()): 48 passed (SURVIVED)
